headline: Allowed Algonquin Gas changes at 96 Tower Road without amended filing; approved trench drain work at 590 Lincoln Street.
summary: Commissioners agreed that changes at 96 Tower Road can go into the as-built plans, with no amended filing. At 590 Lincoln Street, the plan removes a trench drain damaged by plows and pitches the pavement to an existing catch basin.
decisions: Approved a Positive 2B/Negative 3 determination for removal of a trench drain at 590 Lincoln Street, 5-0.
Approved changes to the as-built plans at 96 Tower Road in place of an amended filing, 5-0.
Approved the minutes of the 10-8-2026 meeting, 5-0.

decision_titles: Trench drain removal at 590 Lincoln Street
Changes to as-built plans at 96 Tower Road
plain_text:
Approved 11-5-2026 
  
 
Waltham Conservation Commission 
October 22, 2026 
Meeting Minutes 
Meeting took place via public Zoom call with participation information posted at City Hall, Government 
Center, and on the Commission’s page of the city web site. Zoom information was circulated directly 
to all applicants and others on the public agenda. 
Meeting called to order at 7:05 PM. 
Attendees: Chair Bill Doyle, Gerard Dufromont, Michael Donovan, Anja Shafer, Frank Fitzgerald. 
Conservation Agent Julia Abbott. 
Absent: Vice Chair Lisa Limonciello. 
Public Meeting 
Request for Determination of Applicability 
Applicant: Hobbs Brook Real Estate LLC / Peter Marino 
Property Location: 590 Lincoln Street 
Project Description: Removal of a trench drain and restoration of driveway pavement. Straw wattles 
and silt fence are proposed to minimize disturbance to adjacent areas. 
Anthony Donato of Hancock Associates was present for the applicant. He described work approved 
and completed in 2023 to correct a flooding and icing condition at this location. Curbing, a trench 
drain, and a separator were added. The curbing has worked well, but the trench drain has been 
damaged by plows. The current plan proposes to remove the trench drain and pitch the pavement to 
the existing catch basin, which is expected to work just as well. There will be no increase to 
impervious area. Ms. Abbott noted that Cambridge Water Department approves, as there will be no 
change to quantity or quality of water being treated. She recommended a Positive 2B/Negative 3 
determination. Motion by Ms. Shafer to issue a Positive 2B/Negative 3 determination. Seconded by 
Mr. Donovan. In favor: Doyle, Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. Mr. Doyle 
asked when this would happen. Mr. Donato hoped to complete the work before the bituminous plants 
close down for the winter. 
 
Public Meeting 
Informal Discussion (Relating to DEP 316-0847) 
Applicant: Brad Wynnemer / Algonquin Gas 
Property Location: 96 Tower Road 
Description: Applicant has proposed several changes. Overall reduction of planned work. Discussion 
and recommendation. 
Ms. Abbott described changes proposed by the applicant. She brought this to the commission’s 
attention to confirm that capturing the changes in the as-built plans when the RCOC is submitted will 
be sufficient, and the commission will not request an amended filing. The changes will include a new 
valve station on a 34’×34’ gravel pad with security fence and landscape plantings, reducing the 24” 
line to an 8” line, and no longer needing the retaining wall coordinated with BXP’s adjacent project. 
Cambridge Water has reviewed and requests that all plantings be native. Brief discussion. The
Approved 11-5-2026 
commission agreed that since there is an overall reduction to the permitted work, no amended filing 
will be needed. Mr. Donovan asked that the applicant provide the revised plans for the file. Mr. 
Dufromont suggested the commission take a vote for the record. Motion to allow these changes in the 
as-built, in lieu of filing an amendment, by Ms. Shafer, seconded by Mr. Fitzgerald. In favor: Doyle, 
Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. 
 
Commission Business 
• Approval of meeting minutes from 10- 8-2026. Motion to approve by Ms. Shafer, seconded by 
Mr. Donovan. In favor: Doyle, Donovan, Shafer, Fitzgerald, Dufromont. Motion passed. 
 
Correspondence 
• NOTED: DCR was able to perform unscheduled additional invasive management work in the 
Beaver Brook Reservation the week of 10/5. They expect to submit the annual summary report 
in the near future. [316-0777] 
• NOTED: DEP has moved regional drought status back to “Level 2 – Significant Drought” as of 
October 9. The commission office received a local press inquiry regarding city government 
responsibility for disseminating drought status information, wa ter use recommendations, and 
water restrictions in Waltham. 
• NOTED: Councillor Logan’s report of possible soap or wax residue reaching the Charles River 
from vehicles exiting the car wash on Elm Street. Ms. Abbott has reached out to the owner. She’ll 
follow up next week. 
• NOTED: Charles River Watershed Association has asked conservation commissions in the region 
to issue letters of support on their action to block combined sewer overflow into the Charles 
River in Cambridge and Somerville. Discussion. Commissioners will review and sign individually. 
 
Old Business 
• Conservation Restrictions. Update. The commission will hold off on further review until the next 
meeting (11/5). At the 10/8 meeting, the commission requested that the Law Department be 
asked if a list of potential CR holders exist, and if so if that list can be made available. Mr. Daly 
reported that the Law Department redirected this inquiry to the mayor’s office. The commission 
office has not yet received a response. 
 
Site Visit Reports 
• 44 Shore Road. Resident report of potential dumping (construction debris). Ms. Abbott made a 
site visit on 10/19. She noted mulch, sand, and gravel. The property is for sale and she has 
made contact with the real estate agent. She is trying to reach the contractor to ask them to 
remove the debris. This is at one of the entrances  to the Hardy Pond Conservation Area. Brief 
discussion. Commissioners recommended that Ms. Abbott inform CPW and the Rec 
Department, who also have jurisdiction or interest here. Possibly the police, as an illegal dumping 
violation. Mr. Dufromont recommended the realtor be talked to as they might have had the work 
done. An enforcement order could be pursued. Ms. Abbott also noted that the listed owner is an 
investment LLC, so staying on the agent might be the best approach.  
• Lyman Estate [185 Lyman Street, DEP 316- 0734]. Mr. Donovan visited 10/21 and circulated 
photos. He thinks the new plantings look good. Ms. Abbott also visited recently. She said that 
the RCOC is expected soon. 
 
Committee Reports 
• CPC: Next meeting scheduled for November 17.
Approved 11-5-2026 
New Business 
• Noting the passing of Louis Andrews, former commission member. 
• Possible scheduling of Paine/Storer boundary walk  (Nov./Dec.). To be discussed at the next 
meeting. 
 
Motion to adjourn by Mr. Shafer, seconded by Mr. Dufromont. All present in favor. Motion passed. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:35 PM.
